note: These are common explanations and investigation hints, not a diagnosis of the original C source.

sources.title: GCC optimization options: register pressure and live ranges

register.cause: Often register allocation: the compiler kept the value in a different physical register. Temporary lifetimes, expression order, surrounding calls and optimization settings can affect this choice.
register.check: Trace where the tested value is produced in both versions. Compare local types, expression structure and compiler flags. Renaming a C variable does not directly select its register.

valueRegisters.cause: v0 and v1 can hold expression results and return values under the usual MIPS calling convention. Seeing v1 instead of v0 here does not by itself establish a different return type.
valueRegisters.check: Inspect the instructions that produce the value and any preceding call before changing the C.

fixedRegister.cause: A fixed-purpose register changed, so this may change the value or address being used rather than merely rename a temporary. zero is constant zero; sp is the stack pointer; gp is the global pointer; ra holds a return address.
fixedRegister.check: Verify the value/address provenance, calling convention and context before assuming the change is harmless.

stackOffset.cause: Different stack offsets often reflect a different frame layout: local sizes/order, alignment, spills, saved registers or outgoing call arguments.
stackOffset.check: Compare the stack-frame allocation and neighboring loads/stores, then check local types and compiler settings.

memoryOffset.cause: A changed memory offset can come from a different structure field, array index, element size, pointer type or symbol address.
memoryOffset.check: Check declarations and address calculations, including relocation/symbol information. Do not assume a register-only difference.

globalPointer.cause: A changed gp-relative offset can reflect small-data placement or symbol/global-pointer settings.
globalPointer.check: Check the host symbol addresses, global-pointer setup and -G compiler settings.

branchTarget.cause: Different branch/jump destinations can reflect code layout, added/removed instructions or a different control-flow path.
branchTarget.check: Compare destination blocks and relative displacements. A changed printed address alone does not prove the condition is wrong.

immediate.cause: A changed constant can come from literal values, type width/signedness, structure layout, address relocation or optimizer transformations.
immediate.check: Check how this instruction uses the constant and trace the corresponding C expression before editing a literal.

encoding.cause: The decoded text is the same, but the machine words differ. A hidden encoding field, alias or disassembler formatting may conceal the distinction.
encoding.check: Inspect the raw instruction words and compiler/assembler settings; identical printed text is not an exact byte match.
